about: AgentNet builder bench HOLDOUT: same rules as tasks.json. Never in any model context (every repository read/search tool refuses scripts/bench/holdout*); only the controller reads its scores. Chosen deterministically: the 4 of the original 12 tasks with the smallest sha256(id), then the mined tasks whose sha256(id) starts with 0-3 (mine.py). External holdout tasks: holdout_external.json.

tasks.task: The public-surface monitor records a '<source>:placeholders' observation for a crawled navigation page only when the page has dead '#' or 'javascript:' links, so an incident opened for a page that later becomes clean never receives a healthy sample and can never recover. Make every crawled navigation source emit its '<source>:placeholders' observation: failing (PLACEHOLDER_LINK) when it has dead links, healthy otherwise. Do not change what counts as a dead link.

The maintenance release preview refuses a repair unless every monitored public-surface contract item passes on the preview, so any other defect still open in production blocks the first repair. Judge the preview like post-deploy verification: using the release's recorded production baseline probe, fail only when an item that was healthy in the baseline fails on the preview (an item unknown to the baseline counts as healthy), and separately require the repaired incident's own item to be healthy on the preview. Leave the other preview checks unchanged.

Society dispatch wakes an event's targeted agent and also every role subscribed to the event type, so each repository read result wakes bystanders and burns the story's run budget. An event targeted at one agent must wake only that agent, never also the subscribers of its type.

The Phase 5 live driver cannot show the memory a role carries into its next run. Add a read-only 'memory:<role>' plan step that reports how many live memory rows the role carries and where they came from, scrubbed and without ever reading memory contents, and make the plan grammar accept a memory role and reject junk.

fix(worker): conditional starlette import so worker container starts Phase B's logging_config.py shipped four byte-identical copies, one per service. The file imported ``starlette.middleware.base.BaseHTTPMiddleware`` unconditionally for the RequestIDMiddleware. The registry / payment / simulation containers carry FastAPI (and therefore starlette as a transitive dep), but the worker image only installs sqlalchemy / redis / opentelemetry / prometheus-client / structlog — no starlette. Result on staging deploy: ``agentnet-staging-worker`` crash-looped with ``ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'starlette'``. Fix: guard the starlette import behind a try/except at module top so ``setup_logging`` is callable in any service.

Phase 5 closure: the real-domain driver step and what the live Society actually did (#23) * Phase 5 closure: prove multi-agent operation on a REAL domain signal A synthetic canary proves the runtime; only a real platform fact proves the product. Gate A runs 12/14/16 showed the live Scout declining a synthetic anomaly precisely because it carried no failure artifacts, task ids or logs — which is correct restraint, not a runtime defect.

Maintenance builder: keep 3 reads per try (live bench: 12 spent the turns reading) Bench x3 on staging, same model: this context with 12 reads gave pass@1 0.361 (15/36 turn_budget); with 3 reads 0.778, pass@3 0.917.
